title: SharePoint: create, upload and publish HTML pages, with Copilot drafting
summary: Hold: the briefing says Copilot licensing does not govern HTML uploads, but the sources do not establish that exemption. The rollout, default state and four control paths and commands are supported; narrow the upload statement to the documented licensing gap.

claims.quote: Existing PowerShell settings remain in effect until November 1, 2026. After November 1, 2026, manage availability by using Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control over organization-wide discovery and Microsoft Copilot discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. When you turn on the setting, Microsoft 365 search systems propagate it so that content from the site doesn't appear in organization-wide discovery experiences.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes the Copilot button, AI actions menus and Create pages with AI entry points.
claims.quote: Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: When Restricted Content Discovery is enabled, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions do not appear on the site.
claims.quote: If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires organizational Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId, and empty RemoveLicenses assigns a user licence.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: License Administrator or User Administrator is the minimum role for assigning licences.

claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
